title: Ladder Safety for Painters: Prep Before You Step
summary: Four Massachusetts house painters died in ladder falls in 2011 and 2012. Pick the right ladder, check it, set it up correctly, and use it the right way.
talking_points: Choose a ladder that can hold you and your tools, and check its duty rating label. If a task cannot be done safely from a ladder, use scaffolding or a lift.
Inspect the ladder before each use. Look for cracked, loose, or slippery rungs, split side rails, worn shoes, and rung locks that do not work.
If a ladder has any defect, take it out of service right away and mark it defective or tag it "Do not use."
Set the base on dry, level, secure ground. Set the angle at one foot out for every four feet of ladder height, and secure the base and top.
When you use an extension ladder to get to an upper level, it should extend three feet above the roof edge.
Use a tool belt or hoist to carry materials, and secure your paint to the ladder so you keep a hand free to hold on.
Face the ladder and keep three points of contact while you climb and paint. Keep your belt buckle between the side rails and do not overreach. Climb down and move the ladder instead.
Do not work from the top three rungs of an extension ladder or from the top or top step of a step ladder.
site_hazards_to_check: Bent rungs, damaged side rails, or worn feet
Ladder set on composite decking or soft or uneven ground
Ladder not tied off or secured at the top or base
Extension ladder that does not reach 3 feet above the roof edge
Painter carrying a paint bucket up the ladder
Work that is too high or too far to reach from a ladder
discussion_questions: Is this the right ladder for this job, and has it been inspected today?
How is the ladder secured at the top and bottom, and is the angle right?
What can we use besides a ladder for this task?
